rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 and Tables 1-3 report the authors' own greenhouse spectroradiometer measurements of healthy and inoculated sugar beet leaves, development of four spectral disease indices, 8-fold cross-validated classification results, and application to an independent field dataset and hyperspectral images.
rows.notes: The study shows disease detection and identification, not pest control. Its own results: SDIs classified healthy/Cercospora/rust/powdery mildew leaves with balanced accuracies of 89%, 92%, 87%, 85% (Table 1); SDIs outperformed common SVIs on the controlled-environment data (Table 3: HI 89.0% vs NDVI 80.3%; CLSI 92.4% vs NDVI 73.4%; SVIs 50% for rust and mildew); the health index applied to field canopy spectra reached 81.63% (Section 3.4, Fig. 5), but no SVI comparison was made on field data and disease-specific differentiation was not possible in the field because of mixed infections. No management action, disease control or loss reduction was measured, so the study supports only the detection precondition of the pest_control claim. Authors note difficulties at low severities (1-9%) and the need to re-optimize thresholds per dataset, but these concern detection, not control.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 and Tables 1-3 report the authors' own greenhouse reflectance measurements, index development, cross-validated classification accuracies, and tests on independent field and imaging datasets.
rows.notes: The study reports no crop production, yield or fruit quality outcome. It shows only that spectral disease indices detect and differentiate sugar beet leaf diseases more accurately than common vegetation indices on controlled-environment leaf data (Table 3) and that the health index classifies diseased canopy areas in one field dataset with 81.63% accuracy (Fig. 5). Any link to avoided yield losses is an inference by the review, not a result of the study; detection is a precondition of the crop_production claim.

notes: Full text available including methods, results, discussion and references; supplementary appendices (feature selection details, imaging classification details) not included. Both rows share the same passage; the study supports the detection-accuracy statement on greenhouse data but only partially under field conditions (single field, one date, HI only, no SVI comparison in the field, no disease-specific differentiation due to mixed infections).
